subject: DPA: Territory-specific retention & sunset language — questions
messages:
From: Jacob Simon <jacob.simon@clearline.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Clearline Legal <legal@clearline.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on territory-specific retention + sunset language

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending over the DPA v3. Our GC had two items we want to confirm before we proceed:

1) Territory carveouts — we need explicit wording that customer data for EU customers will be stored and processed within the EU unless otherwise agreed. Your current draft references "regional controls" but doesn't give a clear residency commitment or an exception flow.

2) Sunset/retention interplay — our retention schedule requires that when a customer terminates, their primary data be deleted within 30 days; however our operations team needs a short grace period to extract billing/audit logs (we asked for 60 days). We see your 90-day snapshot retention for disaster recovery and want to understand whether that conflicts with an enforceable delete requirement.

I've attached our annotated redline (Clearline_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) and a short retention matrix. Can you confirm Redwood's stance on both points and suggest contract wording that works for both sides?

Best,
Jacob Simon
Head of Security Programs
Clearline Financial

(attachment: Clearline_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf); retention_matrix_clearline.xlsx (xlsx))

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Jacob Simon <jacob.simon@clearline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on territory-specific retention + sunset language

Jacob —

Appreciate the clear notes and the annotated DPA. High-level answers up front:
- Residency: Redwood can commit to EU resident processing for EU customer accounts; we support a contract clause that requires EU-hosted production workloads and backups inside EU zones (exceptions documented via a customer-approved exception process).
- Sunset vs snapshots: We operate a tiered retention model. Primary data deletion within 30 days is possible for account-scoped user data. Backups/snapshots are retained for up to 90 days for disaster recovery in the default configuration, but we can offer a contractual commitment to delete account-associated snapshots within 60 days post-termination for customers requiring faster erase, with an operational onboarding runbook to verify.

I'll loop Karthik and Marissa to propose concrete clause language and to map operational steps (notification, verification, evidence). Can you confirm Clearline's minimum acceptable snapshot window (30/60/90)?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Jacob Simon <jacob.simon@clearline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on territory-specific retention + sunset language

Jacob / Laura —

Thanks — a few technical clarifications and a proposed redline snippet below. I verified with infra that EU-only hosting for production and nightly backups is supported for Clearline's account based on their committed region. Two operational caveats:

- Cross-border telemetry: some small operational telemetry (aggregated metrics and anonymized health pings) may be routed through non-EU control planes for monitoring. We can contractually limit telemetry to non-identifiable aggregates and provide the telemetry retention floor (30 days) — we will include an evidence/compliance page.

- Snapshots & backups: Our snapshot process uses incremental segments and we perform periodic consolidations. Deleting account primary blobs within 30 days is straightforward. For snapshots, the deletion request triggers a three-step process (de-duplication pass, tombstone, purge). For a 60-day contractual window we can provide a verifiable purge timeline and a delete certificate. 30-day snapshot purge is operationally risky for certain customer-size snapshots because of restoration SLAs; 60 days is our recommended compromise.

Proposed DPA language (suggested insertion to Section 4.a — Data Residency & Retention):

"Customer Data Residency: Redwood Inference shall store and process Customer Data for Customer accounts provisioned in the European Union within EU data centers, except as required for (i) customer-authorized exports, (ii) lawful requests under applicable law, or (iii) aggregated, non-identifiable operational telemetry necessary to maintain service. Redwood shall document any exception and obtain Customer's written approval prior to cross-border processing of Customer Data.

Retention and Sunset: Upon Customer's termination or written request for deletion, Redwood will delete Customer's primary account data within thirty (30) days. Snapshots and backup artifacts containing Customer Data shall be scheduled for purge within sixty (60) days of termination, and Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate within ninety (90) days of completion of the purge process. Exceptions for legal hold or regulatory retention obligations shall be honored and documented."

Let me know if this balances Clearline's needs. I can attach a short ops runbook that maps the 3-step purge to specific job ids and verification artifacts.

—Karthik
Senior Engineer, Infrastructure
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Jacob Simon <jacob.simon@clearline.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Clearline Legal <legal@clearline.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on territory-specific retention + sunset language

Laura / Karthik —

Thanks for the thoughtful proposal and the drafted clause. Clearline is comfortable with the residency wording as long as the exception flow is clearly documented (we'll need that as an appendix). Regarding the snapshot timeline: 60 days purge + signed deletion certificate within 90 days is acceptable to Legal, provided you include an explicit assurance that intermediate backup copies (cloud-provider managed snapshots outside Redwood control) are accounted for in the purge flow. Can you confirm that Redwood's 3-step purge will cover provider-level snapshots and include the provider snapshot ids in the deletion certificate?

If yes, we're happy to proceed with this redline and will circulate an internal sign-off. I'll attach the annotated PDF with two minor edits (highlighted).

Regards,
Jacob Simon
Head of Security Programs
Clearline Financial
(attachment: Clearline_DPA_v3_redline.pdf with minor highlights)
